tier_reason: The README numbers match the output of tests/benchmark.c at commit a9e8fe5 (1e9 iterations, 10 functions), but that harness times 8 independent AVX2 lanes on inputs in about [0, 2] against a serial libm chain total += f(total) seeded with the SIMD time in milliseconds (e.g. 723.73), so acosf/asinf run on |x|>1 and then NaN, expf/exp2f overflow to +inf after one call, and sinf/cosf get arguments near 880. The ratios therefore compare throughput on easy inputs with latency on degenerate inputs; with compiler and CPU model also unstated they are directional only.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O3 -mavx2 -mfma for the benchmark targets (tests/CMakeLists.txt, non-MSVC); compiler of the README run not stated (CI builds with clang on ubuntu-latest and the default compiler on macos-latest)
corrections.workload: tests/benchmark.c (README run matches commit a9e8fe5, NUM_ITERATIONS 1,000,000,000; current code uses 200,000,000): the AVX2 loop evaluates 8 independent lanes starting at 0..0.875 and stepping by FLT_EPSILON (inputs stay in about [0, 2]); the C std loop calls acosf/asinf/atanf/cbrtf/cosf/sinf/expf/exp2f/logf/log2f through a function pointer in a serial dependency chain total += f(total), seeded with the SIMD time in ms.
corrections.caveats: Baseline harness is not like-for-like: the SIMD side is a throughput loop over 8 independent lanes with inputs in about [0, 2], while the libm side is a latency-bound serial chain total += f(total) seeded with the SIMD time in milliseconds (README run, commit a9e8fe5), so acosf/asinf received |x|>1 and then NaN for the whole run, expf/exp2f overflowed to +inf after the first call and sinf/cosf ran on arguments near 880 (current code seeds with seconds, but log2f still drops to NaN and acosf/asinf still leave the domain after one or two calls). The 2.06x-18.14x ratios are therefore not a valid measure of speed against libm. Compiler, libm (glibc or Apple) and CPU model of the README run are not stated ('old Intel Core i7 from 2018'). The author writes 'Performance is not the focus.' The benchmark source is tests/benchmark.c (not visible in the repo root). Fast-mode gains (~1.4x-1.9x for sin, cos, acos, asin, exp2, pow) are against the library's own precise mode. No comparison with SLEEF or xsimd math (both catalogued).

notes: Numbers on the README are real program output, but the benchmark compares 8-lane SIMD throughput on in-range inputs with a serial libm chain that runs on NaN/inf or large arguments, so ratios are confounded (crippled-baseline precedent, like AssemblyScript and dp::thread_pool, rather than a reject). Metadata confirmed: MIT (LICENSE 2025), 38 stars, last commit 2025-11-23 ('updated license'), active. Directionally plausible as an AVX2/NEON transcendental header, but should be shown only as D.

tier_reason: First-party README table with CPU models; the benchmark code (tests/benchmark.cpp) is public and shows the unlabelled baseline is the Wikipedia d2xy implementation, but the compiler and version are not stated and the per-ISA build flags behind the columns cannot be reproduced from the public CMakeLists.txt, so not A.

corrections.baseline: Wikipedia d2xy/rot C implementation (in source/qHilbert.cpp), called once per index from tests/benchmark.cpp; the README table does not label it
corrections.workload: tests/benchmark.cpp: map all 16,384 indices of an order-7 (128x128) Hilbert curve to 2D points, 10 trials averaged with std::chrono::high_resolution_clock, output checked against d2xy (PASS/FAIL). qHilbert2D uses the Hacker's Delight (Lam-Shapiro/Steele) parallel-prefix method, with pext under BMI2 and SSE4.2/AVX2/AVX-512 paths.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMakeLists.txt: -Ofast -Wall -Wextra on the GCC branch, plus -mbmi2 / -msse4.2 / -mavx2 / -mavx512f per Benchmark-* executable; compiler and version not stated
corrections.caveats: The table's baseline (Wikipedia d2xy, branchy loop with one cross-translation-unit call per point and no LTO) is not labelled on the README; it is identified from tests/benchmark.cpp. Most of the gain is algorithmic (Hacker's Delight parallel-prefix rewrite): the Serial/BMI2 column is already x42.5 on i9-7900x, AVX-512 adds about 1.19x over it (derived from page data), and AVX2 is slower than SSE4.2 on E5-2697 v4. In the public CMakeLists.txt the per-target ISA flags are PRIVATE to the Benchmark-* executables (tests/benchmark.cpp) and do not reach the qHilbert static library (source/qHilbert.cpp) that holds the SIMD paths, so a build as written runs the same generic serial code in every target; the flags actually used for the table's columns are not public. Each trial is only 16,384 points (microsecond-scale timing). Compiler not stated. 2018 numbers; repo abandoned since 2018-12-31.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly; baseline is the Wikipedia d2xy loop, so the 9.7x-50.4x speedups are mostly an algorithm change (constant-time parallel prefix) rather than SIMD. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 38 stars, 10 forks, last commit 2018-12-31, abandoned. Category fit is loose (Hilbert-curve index mapping, not a general SIMD intrinsics library).

corrections.claimed_speedup: From the raw google/benchmark max aggregates in RESULTS.md (2026-05-19, derived from page data): default simditoa::to_chars (heterogeneous) vs std::to_chars on the realistic subset: UNIFORM_POS 186.2M vs 54.9M ints/s (3.39x), LOG_HEAVY 135.3M vs 39.6M (3.42x), FIXED:12 189.8M vs 99.9M (1.90x), FIXED:16 189.7M vs 74.0M (2.57x), FIXED:19 186.2M vs 59.4M (3.13x); geomean 176.0M vs 62.5M (2.82x). The specialized homogeneous variant reaches 295.7M / 295.6M / 239.8M at FIXED:12/16/19 (4.04x at 19 digits) but drops to 65.9M on LOG_HEAVY. Batch API (to_chars_batch) geomean 186.1M vs std::to_chars batch 58.0M (3.21x). Signed: UNIFORM 101.2M vs 43.3M (2.34x), LOG 80.1M vs 43.9M (1.83x). Slower than std::to_chars at FIXED:1 (267.3M vs 402.5M) and FIXED:4 (225.4M vs 319.6M), faster at FIXED:8 (225.3M vs 149.5M). Fastest other contender on the realistic subset is yy_itoa (geomean 136.3M; simditoa default 1.29x ahead), and yy_itoa beats simditoa on signed UNIFORM (128.6M vs 101.2M). RESULTS.md's own headline (219M vs 105M geomean) mixes the homogeneous and heterogeneous variants and mislabels columns.

corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark (separate repo by the same author, run by a GitHub Actions workflow on one GCP c3-standard-8 VM). The RESULTS.md prose and tables were written by OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini and mislabel columns: per the D_ enum in common/bench_data.hpp (dist 3 = UNIFORM_POS, dist 4 = LOG_HEAVY), the headline 'UNIFORM_POS' column actually holds FIXED:1 numbers and the 'LOG_HEAVY' column holds UNIFORM_POS numbers, and simditoa's FIXED:12/16/19 headline cells come from the specialized homogeneous variant, so the 219M geomean mixes variants; use the raw output at the bottom of the file. Requires AVX-512 IFMA + VBMI (Ice Lake or Zen 4 and later); the scalar fallback was not benchmarked. Slower than std::to_chars at 1-4 digit outputs, and slower than jeaiii, yy_itoa, rapidjson and fmt at 1-8 digits. Algorithm from Champagne Gareau & Lemire, arXiv:2604.26019 (not checked; arXiv blocked here).
